 Order
As the controversy involved in these Arbitration Appeals is identical, therefore, they are being
disposed of by this common order.

entities.text: National Highway Authority of India (Ministry of Road Transport and Highways) V/s. Bhujbal Singh & another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Appellant/National Highway Authority of India has filed these appeals under Section 37(1)(C) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (for brevity, 'the 1996 Act') being aggrieved by order dated 31/1/2021 (Annexure A/1) whereby the IV Additional District Judge, Shivpuri has allowed the application under Section 34 of the 1996 Act by remanding the matter to the Divisional Commissioner, Division Gwalior for reassessment of the compensation.
(2). Respondents are the owner of the land which was acquired by the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) for the purpose of widening/Four Lane of NH3 from Shivpuri to Dewas Junction.
(3). The Land Acquisition officer passed an Award on 18/1/2013 (Annexure A/4) granting compensation for the acquired land.

(3.1) Being dissatisfied with the aforesaid Award, the land owners approached the Divisional Commissioner, Division Gwalior who is an Arbitrator under Section 3(G)(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (for brevity the 1956 Act').
Learned Arbitrator v i d e Award dated 5/12/2016 (Annexure A/7) has dismissed the application and confirmed the Award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer.

(3.2). Being aggrieved by the aforesaid Award, respondents/land owners filed an application under Section 34 of the 1996 Act before the District Judge, Shivpuri along with an application for condonation of delay.
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) appeared and filed the reply as well as written submissions.

Vide impugned order dated 13/01/2021, the learned IV Additional District Judge, Shivpuri has set aside the Award dated 5/12/2016 (Annexure A/7) and remanded the matter back to the Divisional Commissioner, Division Gwalior for adjudication.
Hence, these appeals are before this Court under Section 37(1)(C) of the 1996 Act.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for appellant submits that the impugned order liable to be set aside on two grounds; firstly that the learned Court in exercise of power under Section 34 of the 1996 Act can not remand the matter since as per language of Section 34 of the 1996, the Court can either set aside or modify the award and secondly, the Additonal District Judge at Shivpuri had no territorial jurisdiction to entertain an application under Section 34 of the 1996 Act.

The land owners ought to have approached the District Court at Gwalior to challenge the Award passed by the Commissioner,
Division Gwalior.

(5). Learned counsel appearing for respondents submits that the High Court while entertaining the appeal under Section 37(1)(C) of the 1996 Act is having power to remand the matter back to the Divisional Commissioner, Division Gwalior for fresh adjudication as the Divisional Commissioner,
Division Gwalior has wrongly dismissed the application filed under Section 3(G)(5) of 1956 Act without considering the material available on record.
(6). During pendency of these proceedings, now the Central Government vide notification dated 3/1/2022 has empowered the District Collector as an Arbitrator under Section 3(G)(5) of 1956 Act.

(7). So far as issue of jurisdiction is concerned, at that time, the Divisional Commissioner, Division Gwalior was the Competent Authority because the land & National Highway both are situated within the divisional jurisdiction of the Commissioner, Division Gwalior.
It is also correct that Additional District Judge has no authority under Section 34 of the 1996 Act to remand the matter.

Learned Additional District Judge ought to have assessed the compensation, if required, on the basis of material/evidence available on record but in the present case as the learned Arbitrator did not enhance the amount of compensation.

Therefore, keeping in the facts of the case in totality, both the Award dated 18/1/2013 ( Annexure A/4) & 5/12/2016 (Annexure A/7) are hereby set aside and the matter is remanded back to Collector, Shivpuri, to decide the application filed under Section 3(G)(5)
of the 1956 Act in accordance with law.
(8). With the aforesaid, the present Arbitration Appeals are disposed of.
A copy of this order be retained in each of the connected Arbitration Appeals.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Appellant/National Highway Authority of India has filed these appeals under Section 37(1)(C) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (for brevity, 'the 1996 Act') being aggrieved by order dated 31/1/2021 (Annexure A/1) whereby the IV Additional District Judge, Shivpuri has allowed the application under Section 34 of the 1996 Act by remanding the matter to the Divisional Commissioner, Division Gwalior for reassessment of the compensation.
(3.1) Being dissatisfied with the aforesaid Award, the land owners approached the Divisional Commissioner, Division Gwalior who is an Arbitrator under Section 3(G)(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (for brevity the 1956 Act').
(3.2). Being aggrieved by the aforesaid Award, respondents/land owners filed an application under Section 34 of the 1996 Act before the District Judge, Shivpuri along with an application for condonation of delay.
opennyai_summary.arguments: Learned counsel for appellant submits that the impugned order liable to be set aside on two grounds; firstly that the learned Court in exercise of power under Section 34 of the 1996 Act can not remand the matter since as per language of Section 34 of the 1996, the Court can either set aside or modify the award and secondly, the Additonal District Judge at Shivpuri had no territorial jurisdiction to entertain an application under Section 34 of the 1996 Act.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
(7). So far as issue of jurisdiction is concerned, at that time, the Divisional Commissioner, Division Gwalior was the Competent Authority because the land & National Highway both are situated within the divisional jurisdiction of the Commissioner, Division Gwalior.
It is also correct that Additional District Judge has no authority under Section 34 of the 1996 Act to remand the matter.
Learned Additional District Judge ought to have assessed the compensation, if required, on the basis of material/evidence available on record but in the present case as the learned Arbitrator did not enhance the amount of compensation.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, keeping in the facts of the case in totality, both the Award dated 18/1/2013 ( Annexure A/4) & 5/12/2016 (Annexure A/7) are hereby set aside and the matter is remanded back to Collector, Shivpuri, to decide the application filed under Section 3(G)(5)
of the 1956 Act in accordance with law.
(8). With the aforesaid, the present Arbitration Appeals are disposed of.
A copy of this order be retained in each of the connected Arbitration Appeals.
